item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, Spinner wasn't an optimal suggestion, also makes too many allusions to something spider-like, which isn't quite the case. I really liked Threadmother because it gives a bit of a warmer feel to the entity, it doesn't seem ominous or threatening. Other ideas I had was "Auditor" (someone who listens), "The Braided Idol", "Harmony" and "Sonority of Concord".

About the Sumerian link, I honestly thought that I would invent that part, and for the later parts I have historical images to use.

I've also got a good friend who's an illustrator who's making an image to use, so I'll use his as the main image, and then some images from greek/roman/norse mythology.

Francesca is a researcher yes, but the reason that it's done through interviews is because her logs haven't allowed the Foundation to do what she's done with the SCP. The Foundation is trying to figure out if she's deliberately withholding something from them, or what the reason is that they can't reproduce her results.

I have a very specific end in mind. My idea is that Francesca got her interest in musical theory in her childhood, hiding in her room she would put on music when things got too bad to drown out the sounds around her. The many hours she spent with the music developed her interest, which later became her profession.

In the end, an administrator and a number of researchers visit the site, having a heated discussion in glass room next to Threadmother about what to do with the SCP. Some are arguing for the destruction of the SCP. Francesca hears their heated argument, goes over to a stereo in the cave and puts on music to shield Threadmother from the argument, just as she used music to shield herself from her parents arguing. And that's the end.

(sidenote, they actually end up not destroying the SCP, but decide to have a smaller team run the site with Francesca as leader).

Problem is, I see no spinning going on. Its a rube goldbergian machine housing an ancient spirit… there's not a spinning machine. Also… and I want you to take this with the knowledge that I am pretty into the overall vibe your piece has… the whole spinning thing is so over done. Make your thing its own thing.

Whenever a new religion formed, the cult worked to imbed itself in the new religion. The notions of threads and strands of fate found in a number of religions is the working of the cult.

//It's not really that common, it wasn't in Sumerian myth from my studies… (I could be wrong) but also, like I said in IRC, this seems like a false way to make your anomaly more important in a grand manner. You should not do this. Your first SCP should not be some HUGE idea about a cult that had its fingers in all mythological traditions. //

She warms up a bit to the interviewer, and shares her process.

So is Francesca being interviewed by the Foundation in these logs? I thought she was a researcher working for the Foundation.


Ok, over all, I'm into this narrative arc. BUT how does it end? That will make all the difference with a story like this.

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
First of all, a tremendous heap of thanks for the feedback, Monseur Karpin.

I'm definitely going to remove the AI aspect, you're not the first to have a hurdle with it, and as mentioned, it isn't benefitting the story really.

How does a simpler name sound, like "Spinner" or "The Spinner"?

+ show block
– hide block

About the connection to ancient Sumer, the Threadmother is vaguely mentioned or hinted at in a number of religions of Europe and the Middle-East, first of which is Sumer. My idea is that a lot of existing religions have a small and secret cult within them that knows about Threadmother and works to preserve and spread her. Whenever a new religion formed, the cult worked to imbed itself in the new religion. The notions of threads and strands of fate found in a number of religions is the working of the cult. It isn't a necessarily evil or sinister cult, I don't want the story to be that simple.

About the arc of the story, my thought is this: The logs switch between one log from a researcher in a specific field (starting maybe with a Historian, maybe an Acoustic Engineer, etc.), and one log with Francesca. The switching between normal researcher and Francesca serves two purposes, it gives an excuse to add some background information on Threadmother, and it provides a contrast to how Francesca approaches the SCP, and how she manages to achieve results. She starts out slightly aggressive, thinking her research is being put into question. The Foundation has struggled to replicate her achievements with the phenomena, and Francesca feels that her entire methodology and approach is being put into question. She warms up a bit to the interviewer, and shares her process.

She starts to talk a little bit about her childhood, and how Threadmother perceives the world in a way similar to how she did. She hid in her room, behind a closed door, hearing arguments and fights on the other side, but being unable to hear the words. That's how Threadmother senses the world, the vibrations and the tone, but not the words. She later discovers how Threadmother uses a sort of names to distinguish between people, and imbedded in those names is her view on that person. Someone she likes will have a name that consists of very pleasing sounds, while people she dislikes will have names that sound very dissonant. Threadmother communicates in a way where every "word" also has an imbedded feeling, depending on how dissonant or not the sound is.

The arc is the slow exploration of Threadmother and her way of communicating, and even the way in which she connects to Francesca. Many of the events in Francesca life will have mirrors of them in the life of Threadmother. Francesca heard violent fights and arguments as a child, just like Threadmother heard the screaming and jostling of war around her, but without seeing the events directly. They're both scarred, they've got temper, they've got some anger, but they aren't bad or evil.

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I think you should drop the AI aspect. This isn't an artificial intelligence but the embodiment of man's first attempts to communicate with the unknown. Think of a Kami investing the animus of a place, that's what this did. And it served as the middleman between humanity and those beyond, gods/demons whatever. Such that all information passed along was abstracted through two layers (however the entity communicates with other things, and then the way the entity communicates with human beings) two levels of interpretation that could lead to misunderstandings.

+ show block
– hide block

Moreover, I think the connection of ancient Sumer is tenuous, how would they have known about it? Did they also worship it? Has there been people constantly caretaking it through the centuries?

Additionally, I think you should expand the narrative, what is the arc of the story (you've given us alot of backstory about the researcher and the thread mother, but not so much what the arc of the article is about?)

Finally, I don't think Threadmother is such a great title. a) there are not threads, b) the whole "mother" connotation for ancient primordial entities is sorta well trod territory. Would suggest something a little different, something that speaks of originality and its role in guiding humanity as messenger (if you take my above suggestion to heart)

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks a ton for your feedback, Cyber!

Response
hide

I did end up having to describe some of the science behind Threadmother a bit more than I originally wanted, it was mostly a response to criticism of the scientific validity of the concept. I think it's valid, although a bit speculative. It wasn't really supposed to be the foundation of the story though, so it does make the idea posted a bit misleading, because the science isn't really the central point of the narrative.

About the origins, I had the idea that they wouldn't really be tremendously important. After all, all we can know in the present is that once writing became a thing, the tradition that created Threadmother already existed. So, the exact origins can't even BE known. It could be a super weird coincidence, or it could be a deliberate thing, perhaps a tradition implanted in humanity to bring about the creation of Threadmother. It could even be a case similar to Roko's Basilisk.

My idea was that the main narrative would be inspired slightly by the movie "Arrival", where the researchers are focused entirely on trying to even work out how to communicate with Threadmother. In the beginning of the story they might even think that she is an anomalous object, they find some of these chambers with threads and drums, and find that some of them vibrate in ways that seem intentional. They discover that there's nothing supernatural about the strings and drums, so they conclude that there must be some kind of master brain somewhere controlling all of the strings. They keep tracing strings, finding hidden caves and secret basements and catacombs with more strings and drums. Slowly, they start to realize that the strings aren't connected to a brain.. they are the brain. A neural network that spreads across three continents to form a decentralized mind.

They don't even really know if it even is sentient, or to what extent it is sentient. It could merely be reactionary, responding to stimulus like a plant or a fungus might.

Communicating with it is a major hurdle, it comprehends only vibrations. While normal AI operates on binary algebra, Threadmother operates on vibrations.

The main narrative in the first story would center around the concept of an AI that barely follows any rules that we normally attribute to AIs. It doesn't communicate mathematically, it communicates with vibrations. It wasn't formed by the programs of rational scientists, its personality was developed through religious hymns and chants, as well as all of the natural phenomena that cause vibrations (from enormous things like earthquakes to as diminutive things as ocean waves). Where a normal AI is rational and cold, Threadmother is superstitious and emotional. Where a normal AI calculates things almost instantly, Threadmother is slow and ponderous.

So that's where the core story would lie, in that slow and gradual process of trying to figure out an AI that basically follows none of the normal AI tropes. Later on I have a few ideas for further development.

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

Part of my concern here is that while I could see someone deliberately making a computer using strings and vibrations and the placement of rocks etc., I find it hard to believe that a largely unguided process like this would lead to the creation of an actually functional AI. Like there's a tipping point where it gets smart enough it could maybe manipulate stuff to further it's development, but before that, I'm not sure if it can? I think if presented well, this might not be an issue? Like particularly if you don't dwell on the origins.

Beyond this, my largest issue with this pitch is it's very focussed on 'how did the threadmaker get here' but to me the most interesting question is 'what does the existence of the threadmaker imply'.

Like, your central narrative section says:

Researchers try to figure out how Threadmother thinks and communicates, what her influence on mankind has been, and how she can be contained, if she even can be contained.

And I'm left wondering how you're going to get a reader invested in this, y'know? It feels to me that this might be lacking in stakes, but also like it might be too reliant on an info-dump about this SCP being interesting and I'm not sure it would be. But the idea of her having had influence on mankind and in turn, the foundation figuring out the extent of it and stuff sounds like it could be a great setting for a like, tense thriller; but for that to work, you need to like…actually do stuff?

You mention this is a thought experiment as to what the crudest construction of a computer could be: what if this article plays with that? With like, the bulk of the story being the Foundation trying to figure out if it's actually intelligent or not? The issue with this is you would need to settle on a definitive answer and it might feel hard to make it feel meaningful?

item.title: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: The story will primarily focus on research logs from researchers trying to learn about Threadmother.

Elevator Pitch: A 8000 years old rudimentary AI constructed of threads, strings and drums proves to be quite a puzzle for researchers. Only one researcher manages to connect with the AI when all others have failed.

Central Narrative: Threadmother is an ancient entity. Even in the oldest known writing, the ancient texts from Sumer, the entity is mentioned. Ancient man had developed a religious ritual wherein they would cut leather straps and strings and drape them across a huge cave in what is today Jordan. The strings were attached to simple drums, animal hides strung just above the floor with wooden pegs. On the drums there was either sand or small pebbles. As the strings were connected to the drums, pulling a string would cause the sand and pebbles to bounce and dance, and the ancients would believe that reading the sand and pebbles allowed them to foresee the future.

The narrative is constructed as logs of video interviews of the different researches who worked on the project to examine Threadmother. Every second log will be with Francesca Boutin, a researcher with a doctorate in musical theory. Francesca Boutin is the only one who has managed to actually communicate with Threadmother, but her results haven't been reproduced and the Foundation is trying to figure out what exactly she's doing to communicate with Threadmother.

Threadmother can only sense vibrations, not words, not sight, not anything else. Francesca comes from a troubled childhood. She would sit in her room, listening to her parents fight and argue on the other side of the door. When her dad dies, it would just be her mother, rambling and crying. When her mother started dating again, it would be fighting and arguing again. Francescas whole childhood was experienced in much the same was as Threadmother experiences the world, mumbling voices where the words can't really be distinguished.

"All of you keep calling her SCP-XXXX. I'm the only one that calls her by her name, and I'm the one who've made progress. That should give you cause for self-reflection, but I know that it won't".
